key_insight: dLI-RADS combines deep learning with interpretable imaging measurements to estimate hepatocellular carcinoma probability from multiphase CT—not to discover drugs.
clinical_relevance: The method could support imaging-based assessment of small liver lesions, where LI-RADS features can be difficult to evaluate consistently.
method: Analyzes manually segmented liver lesions on multiphase CT.
Combines neural network predictions with quantitative measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features.
Integrates these inputs using logistic regression.
evidence_signal: In a multicenter retrospective study excluding lesions larger than 40 mm, internal lesion-level accuracy was 80% for dLI-RADS versus 74% for LI-RADS, meeting the reported non-inferiority criterion (p = 0.04).
watch_item: Retrospective evaluation and manual segmentation limit workflow readiness; external-test results are not provided in the supplied abstract excerpt.
paper_title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
